Set up Bazel remote cache for CI/release
description: Bazel rebuilds everything from scratch each release (~87s for analyze+build). A remote cache (e.g. BuildBuddy free tier or GCS bucket) would make incremental releases near-instant. Steps: 1) Choose provider (BuildBuddy recommended - free for open source). 2) Create account, get API key. 3) Add to .bazelrc: build --remote_cache=grpcs://remote.buildbuddy.io and build --remote_header=x-buildbuddy-api-key=$API_KEY. 4) Store API key as GitHub secret. 5) Add --remote_header flag in CI/release workflows via env var. Expected savings: ~40-80s per release, ~60-90s per CI run.

title: Explore async notarization to overlap with release steps
description: Currently notarization blocks for ~48s with --wait. Could submit notarization, do GitHub release creation in parallel, then poll for completion and staple. Approach: 1) Submit DMG with 'xcrun notarytool submit' (no --wait), capture submission ID. 2) Create GitHub release with un-stapled DMG. 3) Poll notarytool for completion. 4) Staple ticket to DMG. 5) Update release asset with stapled DMG. Trade-off: adds complexity for ~30s savings. May not be worth it given other optimizations.
